title: National & Regional Parties
lead: India's party system is unique in scale: ==one-party dominance== (1952–67) → ==regional assertion== (1967–89) → ==coalition politics== (1989–2014) → what some scholars call the ==‘second dominant party system’==, contested by a resurgent federal front of regional players.

sections.title: Dynamics Between National and Regional Parties

items: ==Coalition bargaining== — since 1989 regional parties have repeatedly held the balance of power, extracting concessions (special category status, central funds, portfolios) — visible again in 2024 with ==TDP and JD(U)== as key NDA partners.

==Centre–State friction== — clashes over ==fiscal federalism== (GST compensation, devolution), ==Governor's conduct==, and use of ==central agencies (ED, CBI)== in Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Kerala, Punjab.
==Absorption and realignment== — national parties co-opt regional leaders (==Shiv Sena and NCP splinters joining NDA, 2022–23==), reshaping the national/regional distinction itself.
==Vote-bank consolidation== — sub-national coalitions around caste blocs (==Yadav-Muslim in RJD/SP, Maratha in Shiv Sena/NCP==) can override programmatic politics.
==Symbol and identity politics== — post-split symbol disputes (Shiv Sena, NCP) have made the ==ECI's adjudicative role under the 1968 Order== a site of intense contestation.

==National front formations== — regional parties federate periodically (==National Front 1989, United Front 1996, INDIA bloc 2023==), reflecting the ==federalisation== of Indian party politics without full nationalisation of any alternative.
==Criminalisation of politics== — rising share of MPs/MLAs facing charges across both categories; weak enforcement despite [[Lily Thomas (2013)]] and [[Public Interest Foundation (2018)]].
==Dynastic and personality-centred structures== — many regional parties are effectively ==family enterprises== (DMK, SP, RJD, NCP, Shiv Sena, TDP, JD(S)).
==Opaque political funding== — Electoral Bonds struck down in [[ADR v. UoI (Feb 2024)]] for violating ==Art 19(1)(a)==, yet opacity persists via ==electoral trusts and unreported cash==.

==Weak anti-defection enforcement== — Speaker's discretion, no time limits and politically motivated delays ([[Keisham Meghachandra Singh, 2020]]) enabled engineered defections toppling governments in ==Karnataka (2019), MP (2020), Maharashtra (2022)== — disproportionately hitting regional-party-led coalitions.
==Fragmentation and coalition instability== — ==2,800+ registered-unrecognised parties== dilute the meaning of ‘national party’ status; frequent splits fragment regional mandates.

==Regionalism vs national cohesion== — excessive sub-nationalism produces inter-state disputes (==Cauvery, Mullaperiyar==, language imposition) and complicates coordination (GST Council consensus, NEP rollout).
==ECI's limited regulatory teeth== — ==no statutory power to deregister== a party for constitutional violations; the MCC lacks legal backing; ==s.29A registration is largely a formality==.

==Erosion of ideology in favour of patronage== — competition on welfare populism (‘freebies’) and identity mobilisation rather than programmatic differentiation — flagged in [[S. Subramaniam Balaji v. Govt of TN (2013)]].

head: Country
Party system feature
rows: Strong regional parties (==Catalan, Basque==) formally integrated into national coalition bargaining; ==asymmetric federalism== accommodates regional autonomy statutes.
==SNP and Plaid Cymru== function as devolved-national regional parties; ==PPERA 2000== mandates donor transparency.
==Strict two-party dominance== (FPTP + no legal recognition tier for regional parties) suppresses regional party formation despite sub-national diversity.

items: ==Statutory backing for the MCC== — a legally enforceable code with graded penalties, reducing selective enforcement
==Mandatory inner-party democracy== — amend s.29A norms to require ==periodic, ECI-audited internal elections== and transparent succession
==State funding / reformed donation regime== — building on ==Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998)== and the 2024 verdict, a transparent, capped, traceable ==National Election Fund== applying uniformly
==Independent tribunal for anti-defection== — implementing the Keisham Meghachandra Singh suggestion of a ==retired judge-headed, time-bound== mechanism replacing Speaker discretion
==Rationalised recognition criteria== — periodic review of thresholds to prevent both fragmentation and unfair loss of recognition
==Strengthen cooperative federalism platforms== — institutionalise the Inter-State Council and the GST Council consensus model to channel regional demands constructively
==Regulate political advertising and populism== — per S. Subramaniam Balaji, ECI-issued ==fiscal responsibility disclosures== for welfare promises
==Decriminalisation== — fast-track courts for MP/MLA cases to ensure disposal ==before the next election cycle==
